cover.hook: $1.3B — NWO's Marathon mine is fully financed. Construction starts this quarter.
cover.sub: Plus: Canada launches an open-source AI consortium for SMEs, FedNor puts $835K into Northern Ontario, and a new Thunder Bay Indigenous firm targets AI infrastructure equity.

reelSub: $1.3B Marathon mine. Open-source AI for SMEs. FedNor $835K. New Indigenous capital firm in Thunder Bay. Ring of Fire reality check.
storySub: Five developments this week that shape investment, AI access, and the resource economy in Northwestern Ontario.

items.title: Marathon mine fully financed — construction starts in NWO this quarter
items.body: Generation Mining secured $1.3B including $140M from the Canada Growth Fund for the Marathon copper-palladium mine in Northwestern Ontario. 800+ construction jobs. Early works Q4 2026.
items.tease: Next: Canada cuts the cost of AI for small business.
items.reelLine: Generation Mining secured $1.3 billion in full financing for the Marathon mine in Northwestern Ontario — construction begins Q4 2026.

items.title: Canada launches a national open-source AI consortium to cut SME adoption costs
items.body: At ALL IN 2026, Minister Solomon joined Mila, Mozilla, and Hypertec to announce a Canadian-led open-source AI consortium. Goal: lower the price and complexity of AI adoption for small businesses.
items.tease: Next: FedNor directs $835K to Northern Ontario communities.
items.reelLine: Canada's ALL IN 2026 conference launched a national open-source AI consortium to make advanced AI tools cheaper and easier for small businesses.

items.title: FedNor puts $835,777 into 15 Northern Ontario projects — announced in Thunder Bay
items.body: 15 youth employment and Indigenous development projects across Northern Ontario. NWO projects include $100K for Wake the Giant in Thunder Bay, $57.5K each in Lake of the Woods and Sioux Narrows.
items.tease: Next: a new Thunder Bay firm targets First Nations AI equity.
items.reelLine: FedNor announced $835,777 for 15 Northern Ontario projects on September 17 in Thunder Bay, including $100K for Wake the Giant Festival.

items.title: Making Ground River Capital: Thunder Bay Indigenous firm targets AI infrastructure ownership in NWO
items.body: Jason Rasevych (Ginoogaming First Nation) launched Making Ground River Capital at PM Carney's Canada Investment Summit. The Thunder Bay firm focuses on First Nations equity in AI data centres, clean energy, and NWO supply chains.
items.tease: Next: Ring of Fire — real progress, real limits.
items.reelLine: Making Ground River Capital launched in Toronto — a new Thunder Bay-based Indigenous firm pursuing equity ownership in AI infrastructure and NWO supply chains.

items.title: Ring of Fire: two roads approved, the mine is still years away
items.body: Both Marten Falls and Webequie roads cleared assessment in 2026. But the Northern Road Link is still in review, no mine has a final investment decision, and nine First Nations filed a constitutional challenge in 2025.
items.reelLine: Two Ring of Fire access roads have cleared assessment — but no mine has a committed investment decision, and the middle connector road is still awaiting approval.

summary.title: Specific projects are moving; speculative ones are not — and the capital to tell the difference is getting clearer
summary.body: This week Marathon mine went from financed to building; the Ring of Fire remained a long-horizon project with unresolved conditions. Meanwhile, Canada made a structural bet on open-source AI for SMEs, and a Thunder Bay firm moved to put First Nations in the equity seat of the next infrastructure build-out.
